smallest_missing_suppliers.claim: Every decreasing chain sequence of simple nonidentity cycles admits a single finite limiting ambient plaque word with germs identified at approaching basepoints and an embedded nonidentity lobe domain contained in every chain member.

The chosen adjacent annulus has actual C² regular port traces extending to the saddle endpoint in a common transverse coordinate; an immersed endpoint can be glued relative to prescribed regular edge collars.
The selected inward family is connected by compact transverse cap transport to a specific initial plaque cap, or finite null-lobe replacements supply that cap without altering the prescribed family.

local_proof_notes.title: A fixed plaque word preserves nonidentity at approaching basepoints
local_proof_notes.statement: Let H be one holonomy representative defined on an open interval containing 0, with H(0)=0. Let t_n tend to 0. Suppose the holonomy germs of leaf loops c_n, after specified transversal-coordinate identifications, equal the germs of this same H at t_n, and each is nonidentity. Then the germ of H at 0 is nonidentity. In particular this applies to nearby cycles following one fixed finite plaque word, whenever the stated identification is proved.
local_proof_notes.strategy: If the germ of H at 0 were identity, there would be an open interval J about 0 on which H(t)=t. For all sufficiently large n, t_n belongs to J; the germ at t_n is then identity, contradicting the hypothesis. Coordinate conjugacy preserves identity. For a specified finite plaque word, finite plaque transport produces a single representative on a sufficiently small common interval; identifying c_n with that word gives exactly the stated hypotheses. This lemma does not assert that Hausdorff convergence of source cycles supplies such an itinerary.

local_proof_notes.title: Countable choice selects a minimal cycle from finite chains with lower bounds
local_proof_notes.statement: Assume ACω. Let L be a nonempty family of bounded planar cycle domains with finite areas A(D), covered by finitely many inclusion chains. Assume strict inclusion of members has strictly increasing area, and every decreasing sequence in any one chain has a lower bound which belongs to L. Then L has an inclusion-minimal member.
local_proof_notes.strategy: Put a=inf{A(D):D in L}. By ACω choose D_n with A(D_n)<a+1/n. Assign each D_n to the first chain containing it; a chain occurs infinitely often. Take those indices in increasing order and replace its successive terms by their finite inclusion minima. This is a decreasing sequence whose areas tend to a, with no dependent arbitrary choices. Its lower bound E belongs to L, so a≤A(E)≤a and A(E)=a. A proper smaller member would have smaller area, contradicting the definition of a. Crucially, the lower-bound hypothesis includes membership in L, including nonidentity holonomy if L is the nonidentity family; this proof does not establish the geometric lower-bound hypothesis.

local_proof_notes.title: Prescribed plaque port collars admit a C² transverse corner patch
local_proof_notes.statement: Let a C² foliation box have coordinates (y,z) in B×J, with B a convex open ball in R². On two disjoint endpoint collars of an interval, suppose prescribed C² traces have coordinates (Y_-(θ,t),z(t)) and (Y_+(θ,t),z(t)), for t in [0,ε], with z′(t)≠0. Suppose their t=0 collar paths admit a C² joining path E:[0,1]→B equal to Y_-(θ,0), respectively Y_+(θ,0), on slightly larger endpoint collars. Then, after shrinking ε, there is a jointly C² trace on the whole interval agreeing exactly with the prescribed traces on the smaller collars, ending at (E(θ),z(0)), lying in one plaque for each t, and transverse in its t direction. If an original characteristic passage lies in this same plaque box with the same endpoints, the patch is leafwise homotopic to that passage relative to the endpoint collars. No immersion assertion is made.
local_proof_notes.strategy: Choose disjoint C² cutoffs χ_- and χ_+ supported in the larger endpoint collars and equal to 1 on the prescribed smaller collars. Extend χ_±(Y_±(θ,t)-Y_±(θ,0)) by zero beyond their supports; these are jointly C² because the cutoffs vanish on open collars of the support boundaries. Set A(θ,t)=E(θ)+χ_-(θ)(Y_-(θ,t)-Y_-(θ,0))+χ_+(θ)(Y_+(θ,t)-Y_+(θ,0)). At the smaller collars this equals the prescribed Y_± exactly, and at t=0 it equals E. Compactness of E([0,1])⊂B gives a positive margin to ∂B. Uniform continuity makes both correction terms smaller than that margin for sufficiently small ε; hence A stays in B. The trace is (A(θ,t),z(t)); it is C² and its normal t derivative is z′(t)≠0 everywhere. For each positive t, convex linear interpolation between the patch and the original passage gives a plaque-contained homotopy fixing the common endpoint collars. Finite such patches glue on open collars to given regular strips, so their global trace is C². The hypotheses require actual C² port traces extending to t=0 with a common regular transverse coordinate; an abstract graph or a free-homotopy class does not supply them.
